terra.problem: David's statement that he shall not want does not establish that he is currently running short on absolutely nothing.
The picture does not say the sheep has nowhere to be.
“Not yet” implies that danger closes in later, which the valley verse does not say.
The psalm does not say that the grass and water cared for David's outside. It says the LORD makes him lie down in green pastures and leads him beside quiet waters.
The cookie-box joke appears in an explanation about the valley of the shadow of death. Heavy moments have no joke.
The explanation reduces the rod and staff to one stick. David names both.
David names a rod and a staff, not one stick, and does not say either is big.
The psalm does not say David gets a good seat.
The psalm does not say the LORD and David sit down together.
“Table first, nap later” adds a nap to David's account.
The psalm says the table is prepared in the presence of David's enemies. It does not place them in a room.
Floury footprints imply Papa Dorin walks on feet. His gold base is part of him and always comes with him.

explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. David says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." (Psalm 23:1) Not wanting there means not going without what he needs. With the LORD as his shepherd, David isn't running short on anything.

David isn't talking about earning anything in this line. He says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." (Psalm 23:1) The point is he won't go without what he needs. And honestly, if a sheep had to EARN its grass, I'd want to see that sheep's résumé.

Close, but losing would be about something slipping away. David says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." (Psalm 23:1) He's saying he won't go without what he needs. Now me, I lose my oven mitt three times a batch, so I'm no expert in not losing things.

That's the feel, baker. David says, "He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters." (Psalm 23:2) Lying down, soft grass, quiet water. That sheep has nowhere to be, and I have never once seen my oven timer that relaxed.

No hustle in this verse, friend. The sheep is lying down in green pastures and being led beside quiet waters (Psalm 23:2). The only one doing any leading is the shepherd. Hustle is my bakery on a big order day, not this picture.

Not here, not yet. Verse 2 is all green pastures and quiet waters, with the sheep lying down (Psalm 23:2). The dark valley shows up later, in verse 4. And even there, David says, "…I will fear no evil, for You are with me…" (Psalm 23:4)

Right on, baker. David says, "He restores my soul…" (Psalm 23:3) Restore means bring something back to good shape. The grass and water cared for the outside, and now the LORD is caring for the inside too.

David doesn't say tests in this line. He says, "He restores my soul…" (Psalm 23:3) Restore means bring something back to good shape. So far this whole song is the LORD caring for him, one gift after another.

No scales in this verse, friend. The only thing getting weighed around here is my flour, and that's a whole production. David says, "He restores my soul…" (Psalm 23:3) Restore means bring something back to good shape.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His name
explanations.explanation: Exactly, baker. David says, "He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name." (Psalm 23:3) He puts the reason right at the end of the line, like a bow on a cookie box. It's for the LORD's name, plain and simple.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His flock
explanations.explanation: I know, it sounds very shepherd-y. But this verse never mentions a flock. David says the LORD guides him in the paths of righteousness "for the sake of His name." (Psalm 23:3) The reason is the LORD's name.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His land
explanations.explanation: No land in this line, friend. David says the LORD guides him in the paths of righteousness "for the sake of His name." (Psalm 23:3) The paths are about righteousness, and the reason is the LORD's name. Not a single field or border in sight.

explanations.answer: Because the LORD is with him
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. David says, "…I will fear no evil, for You are with me…" (Psalm 23:4) Notice something? Up to now he's been saying "He," and right here in the dark valley he switches to "You." He's talking straight to the LORD now.

David never points to his own strength here. And "alone" is the opposite of what he says: "…I will fear no evil, for You are with me…" (Psalm 23:4) Believe me, I tried carrying six cookie boxes alone once. My mustache is STILL recovering.

The verse never says how long the valley is. It could be a short walk or a long one, and David doesn't tell us. His reason is this: "…I will fear no evil, for You are with me…" (Psalm 23:4) It's who's with him, not how far he has to go.

True, baker. Right there in the dark valley, David says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me." (Psalm 23:4) The thing you might think is scary turns out to be a comfort. That's a good shepherd's stick.

It's actually true, friend. In the valley of the shadow of death, David says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me." (Psalm 23:4) Big stick, scary place, and still it brings him comfort. That stick is on David's side.

You got it, baker. David says, "You prepare a table before me…" (Psalm 23:5) Somebody else setting the table for YOU? That's how you know you're the guest. The LORD is the host, and David gets the good seat.
No tent in this verse, friend. David says, "You prepare a table before me…" (Psalm 23:5) The picture here is a host and a guest sitting down together. A table, not a campsite.
Close, since David did lie down back in verse 2, in green pastures. But here the picture is a host and a guest. David says, "You prepare a table before me…" (Psalm 23:5) Table first, nap later.

Not far away at all, friend. David says, "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies." (Psalm 23:5) His enemies are right there, and the table gets set anyway. Picture sitting down to a party while the folks who doubted you are still in the room.

You caught it, baker. The table isn't far away from his enemies. David says, "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies." (Psalm 23:5) They're right there in the room, and the LORD sets the table anyway.
That's the picture, baker. David says, "…my cup overflows." (Psalm 23:5) That's more than the cup can even hold. My chocolate chip bin does that every time I fill it, and nobody has ever complained.

Nobody's knocking anything over here, friend. David says, "You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows." (Psalm 23:5) That comes right after the LORD prepares him a table. It's a picture of having more than the cup can hold, more than enough.
Nothing in this verse is in a hurry. David says, "…my cup overflows." (Psalm 23:5) That's more in the cup than it can hold. When I'm rushed, I don't get MORE of anything except flour on my apron.

Right, baker. David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life…" (Psalm 23:6) All the days, not just the good ones. The only thing that follows ME around is a trail of floury footprints.
Those two aren't in this line, friend. David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life…" (Psalm 23:6) Goodness and mercy are what he's counting on, every single day.
Good things, but not what David names here. He says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life…" (Psalm 23:6) Goodness and mercy, right behind him, for the rest of his life.

explanations.answer: In the house of the LORD
explanations.explanation: That's how he ends it, baker. David says, "…and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever." (Psalm 23:6) The song started out in a field with a shepherd. It ends with David at home with the LORD, forever.

Hebron is a real place in David's life, where he was king over Judah for seven and a half years (2 Samuel 2:11). But that's not where this song ends. David says, "…and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever." (Psalm 23:6) Seven and a half years is a long time, but forever wins.

Canaan is the land God promised to Abraham's family (Genesis 17:8), but it's not in this song. David closes with, "…and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever." (Psalm 23:6) His forever home is the house of the LORD.
